clue.text: A top man brings in outstanding features

parts.note: the head is the person at the top, as of a school
a headmaster brings in lines, the written punishment set for naughty pupils

explanation.surface: A boss arrives at the office with some striking new features to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' are a British school punishment: copying out a sentence many times, handed out by the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlines are the large-type titles that stand out most prominently on a newspaper page.

clue.text: He has a simple way of dealing with ill-health

definitions.text: He has a simple way of dealing with ill-health

parts.note: surface reading: a man with an uncomplicated approach to illness
setter's reading: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant, so his way of treating illness uses plants

explanation.surface: A man with an easygoing, uncomplicated approach to coping with sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who treats patients with plant-based remedies, once called simples, deals with sickness that way.

clue.text: A move up

parts.note: taken as written
to stir is to move slightly

explanation.walkthrough: 'A move up' reads like a promotion, but 'up' is the definition, in the sense of out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up and about in the morning is out of bed and moving around, which is being astir.

clue.text: Stood idly around — or alternatively toiled without hesitation

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters is wanted, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone either loafed about or worked hard without pausing — two opposite accounts of the same day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, so the hesitation sits with the letters of toiled before they are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about doing nothing in particular, so the past tense matches standing idly around.

clue.text: Neighbouring state

definitions.note: the whole phrase is the definition, a state of being close

parts.note: near means close by, as a neighbour is
-ness is the suffix that turns an adjective into a noun naming a state or condition

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks political, a country next door, but it means a condition, and in the wordplay it is the suffix for one; the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the quality or condition of being close at hand, which is what neighbouring describes.

clue.text: Sound places to get spectacles

indicators.note: sound means the word is taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: sites are places, and the word is pronounced like another spelling

explanation.surface: Advice on reliable shops where you can buy a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles in the sense of remarkable things to see, like the tourist attractions of a city.

clue.text: Skins reversed to reveal the nap

indicators.note: the word for skins is turned back to front

parts.note: peels are the skins of fruit

explanation.surface: Turning animal hides over to show the soft raised pile of the leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nap' looks like the pile on fabric or suede, which suits skins, but it means a doze.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short spell of sleep taken during the day.

clue.text: Bishop in visitation is full of twinkles

indicators.note: in places the bishop inside the word for a visit

parts.note: a stay is a visit somewhere
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop arriving on a visit, his eyes twinkling with good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is Right Reverend, abbreviated RR, rather than the chess B.
explanation.definitionFit: A night sky full of twinkling stars is starry, and eyes bright like stars are too.

clue.text: Probing into a variety of pies over a period

indicators.note: a variety suggests the letters arranged in a different form

parts.note: taken as written
on means over or about, as in a talk on a subject
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A long, drawn-out investigation into an assortment of pies, as if by a food inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is spying, the secret probing into another party's affairs to gather information.

clue.text: Reporters cause harassment

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to harass or urge someone insistently

explanation.surface: Journalists hounding people, a familiar complaint about the media.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names journalists as a body, and the verb means to urge or harry someone persistently.

clue.text: Breaking down in tears — it's the drink

indicators.note: something breaking down falls apart, so its letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing, with the blame placed on what they have been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Contend the Greek wants fruit

parts.note: Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a Greek is hungry for fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with something is to struggle or wrestle with it, which is to contend.

clue.text: A large stretch of water where birds may raise young

parts.note: taken as written
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A big lake where water birds come to breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie, or eyrie, is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, where chicks are reared.

clue.text: No rocky situation before debts become widely known

parts.note: taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor in south-west England
IOUs are written promises to repay, so debts

explanation.surface: Without a crisis, someone's unpaid debts would not become public knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky situation' sounds like a crisis, but it is a literal rocky place.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous, usually for something bad, so known to many people.

clue.text: Being within the fold is swell!

parts.note: in means inside
a crease is a fold line

explanation.surface: A cheerful remark about the joy of belonging to a group, as a sheep in the pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell!' looks like the slang for great, but it is a verb meaning grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger, which is what it means to increase in size or number.

clue.text: A woman's attitude following swindle

indicators.note: following puts the attitude second, after the swindle

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A woman takes a particular view after being cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female first name, so it fits a vague 'a woman' in crossword style.

clue.text: This has a touch of magic

definitions.text: This has a touch of magic

parts.note: surface reading: something slightly enchanting or charming
setter's reading: a conjurer's tool whose literal touch works the magic

explanation.walkthrough: 'A touch of magic' sounds like a hint of charm; read literally, it is an object that performs magic by touching.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's stick is tapped on things to make spells or tricks happen.

clue.text: Such sweetening for freshly-brewed tea's a drug!

indicators.note: something freshly brewed has been newly mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that sugar stirred into a fresh pot of tea is as addictive as a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Date sugar is a sweetener made from dried, ground dates.

clue.text: Firm leader

parts.note: surface reading: a leader who is strict and decisive
setter's reading: firm is a noun, a company, so this is someone who runs one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective for a strong leader, but it is the noun meaning a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's board member who manages its business leads that company.

clue.text: 29 has made dope doubly fashionable

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
doubly says the fool comes twice
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A killer has turned drug-taking into a twice-over trend.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 29, a strangler; 'dope' suggests drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a killer, and an assassin is one too, usually of someone prominent.

clue.text: Can't find shade

parts.note: a tin is a can
the letter left after the apostrophe, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains they cannot find any shade from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't' splits into a can and the letter after the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or slight variation of a colour.

clue.text: A girl restrained but dissipated

parts.note: a miss is a girl
pent, as in pent-up, means held in

explanation.surface: A young woman who kept herself in check yet lived a wild life.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspent youth is one wasted, squandered or dissipated on frivolous things.

clue.text: It is seen in a staff showing courtesy

indicators.note: is seen in means one word appears inside another

parts.note: a pole is a staff
taken as written

explanation.surface: Good manners are evident among a company's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A courteous person is well-mannered and civil, which is being polite.

clue.text: Sticks around Spanish centre or French place

indicators.note: around means the sticks wrap about the other letter

parts.note: canes are walking sticks

indicators.note: centre keeps only the middle letter of the word

parts.note: the fourth of its seven letters

explanation.surface: Choosing between a city in central Spain and one in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The canes split around the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannes is a resort town on the French Riviera, famous for its film festival.

clue.text: Good grounds to set a limit on the beer intake

parts.note: to ration is to limit the amount allowed
ale is the beer being drunk

explanation.surface: A sound reason to cut back on how much beer someone drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or justification behind a decision, its basis in argument.

clue.text: Blue could be appropriate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests sad or rude; in British politics it is the Conservative colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives sit on the political right, and the word also means correct or suitable.

clue.text: A bit of an ordeal to some singers

indicators.note: a bit of means only a part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of ordeal into the next two words

explanation.surface: Some singers find performing a bit of a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos are singers with the low female or high male voice part in a choir.

clue.text: A hearing test

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a case heard in a court of law
second meaning: an experiment or try-out

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an ear examination; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case examining evidence is one meaning; a try-out of something to see how it performs is another.

clue.text: The fellow in a muddle may well make a bloomer

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

indicators.note: a muddle is a mess, so the two short words get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confused man is likely to make an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like British slang for a blunder; here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentian is a flowering plant with vivid blue trumpet-shaped flowers, so it blooms.

clue.text: Trying shirt with a smart appearance

parts.note: surface reading: trying on a shirt in a shop
setter's reading: putting a shirt to the trial to see whether it looks smart

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' reads as trying on clothes; it also means putting something to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something is to put it through a trial or examination of how it performs.

clue.text: The directions given are the ones indicated here

parts.note: taken as written
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Pointing at a set of instructions and saying these are the ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative pronoun points to nearby things, the items being shown here.

clue.text: Foreigner sheltering a trainee 18

indicators.note: sheltering means holding something safely inside

parts.note: a stranger is a foreigner or outsider
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An outsider protecting a newcomer, who turns out to be a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 18, an assassin.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a killer who throttles victims, and an assassin is also a killer.
